title: Solving one-variable equations
blurb: Solve one-variable equations with inverse operations, the distributive property and a final check, including formulas.
question: A lab bill shows a $30 processing fee plus $16 for each test, for a total of $142. The TEAS asks you to solve 16t + 30 = 142 for the number of tests. Which steps do you take, in which order, and how do you know your answer is right?

teach.body: Formally, an equation states that two expressions are equal, and solving it means finding the value of the variable that makes the statement true. In plain English: picture a balance scale with the same weight on each side. Whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other, or it tips. Your goal is to get the variable alone on one side; the number left on the other side is the solution.

steps.label: Clear fractions
steps.sub: Multiply every term by the LCD

steps.label: Collect terms
steps.sub: Variables on one side, numbers on the other

steps.label: Divide
steps.sub: Divide both sides by the coefficient

steps.label: Check
steps.sub: Substitute the answer into the original

teach.body: To build 3x − 7, you multiply x by 3 first and subtract 7 second. To solve 3x − 7 = 11, you undo those steps in reverse: add 7 to both sides (3x = 18), then divide both sides by 3 (x = 6). Think of taking off shoes and socks: the last thing on is the first thing off. Always finish with a check: 3(6) − 7 = 18 − 7 = 11. ✓

teach.caption: Read left to right to build the expression; read right to left to solve it.

items: Distribute to BOTH terms in the parentheses: 4x + 8 = 2x + 18.
Collect the variable terms: subtract 2x from both sides, giving 2x + 8 = 18.
Collect the numbers: subtract 8 from both sides, giving 2x = 10.
Divide both sides by 2: x = 5.
Check in the ORIGINAL: left side 4(5 + 2) = 4(7) = 28; right side 2(5) + 18 = 10 + 18 = 28. ✓

teach.text: The two classic slips: distributing to only the first term (4(x + 2) written as 4x + 2), and dividing only one term by the coefficient (2x + 6 = 10 turned into x + 6 = 5). Exam distractors are built from exactly these slips, and from stopping one step early (choosing 18 from 3x = 18).

teach.h: Solving 2x + 6 = 10: right way versus the slip
teach.caption: Dividing is fine only if EVERY term on both sides is divided. Undo the addition first and the problem disappears.

items: Jasmine, a pre-nursing student, gets a lab bill: a $30 processing fee plus $16 per test, total $142. Let t = number of tests.
Equation: 16t + 30 = 142.
Subtract 30 from both sides: 16t = 112. Check: 112 + 30 = 142. ✓
Divide both sides by 16: t = 7. Check: 16 × 7 = 112. ✓
Final check in the story: 7 tests × $16 = $112, plus $30 = $142. Jasmine had 7 tests.
Solve d = rt for t: t is multiplied by r, so divide both sides by r: t = d/r.
Use it: 150 miles at 60 miles per hour takes t = 150 ÷ 60 = 2.5 hours. Check: 60 × 2.5 = 150. ✓
Solve C = (5/9)(F − 32) for F: multiply both sides by 9/5, then add 32: F = (9/5)C + 32.
No solution: 2x + 3 = 2x + 5 becomes 3 = 5, which is never true.
Infinitely many solutions: 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2 becomes 2 = 2, which is always true.
Do the same thing to both sides, every time.
Order: distribute, clear fractions, combine like terms, collect, divide, check.
Undo operations in reverse order: addition and subtraction before multiplication and division.
Distribute to every term in the parentheses; divide every term by the coefficient.
Check by substituting into the ORIGINAL equation; do not stop at 3x = 18.

summary: You can now solve one-variable equations by undoing operations in reverse order, distributing correctly and collecting terms, and you can rearrange a formula such as d = rt. You can also check every answer by substitution and spot the distractors built from the classic slips.

A.why: Subtract 9 from both sides: 5x = 35. Divide by 5: x = 7. Check: 5(7) + 9 = 35 + 9 = 44. ✓

whyNot.0: 10.6 comes from adding 9 instead of subtracting it: 5x = 53.
whyNot.1: 35 is the value of 5x, one step short of x.
whyNot.3: −0.2 comes from dividing only 44 by 5 (x + 9 = 8.8). Undo the + 9 first.

A.why: Distribute: 4x − 12 = 20. Add 12: 4x = 32. Divide by 4: x = 8. Check: 4(8 − 3) = 4(5) = 20. ✓

whyNot.0: 5.75 distributes the 4 to x only (4x − 3 = 20, so 4x = 23).
whyNot.3: 32 is the value of 4x, one step short of x.

A.why: Add 4 to both sides: x/6 = 6. Multiply both sides by 6: x = 36. Check: 36 ÷ 6 − 4 = 6 − 4 = 2. ✓

whyNot.1: 16 multiplies only x/6 and the 2 by 6, leaving −4 unchanged (x − 4 = 12). Every term must be multiplied.
whyNot.2: 1 divides 6 by 6. To undo division by 6, multiply by 6.

B.why: Distribute: 6x + 2 = 4x + 14. Subtract 4x: 2x + 2 = 14. Subtract 2: 2x = 12. Divide: x = 6. Check: 2(19) = 38 and 4(6) + 14 = 38. ✓

whyNot.1: 1.2 adds 4x to the left instead of subtracting it, giving 10x = 12.
whyNot.3: 8 adds the 2 to 14 instead of subtracting it, giving 2x = 16.

B.q: The simple interest formula is I = Prt. Which expression gives r?
B.why: r is multiplied by P and t, so divide both sides by Pt: r = I/(Pt).

whyNot.1: Pt/I is upside down: it divides Pt by I instead of I by Pt.
whyNot.2: P and t multiply r, so they are undone by division, not subtraction.
whyNot.3: Multiplying I by Pt makes the expression bigger; to undo multiplication, divide.

B.q: A phlebotomy course costs $90 for books plus $115 per week. Kiara paid $895 in total. Solve 90 + 115w = 895 for the number of weeks, w. Round to the nearest tenth if needed.

whyNot.0: 805 is the value of 115w, one step short of w.
whyNot.1: 7.8 divides the full $895 by 115 and ignores the $90 book fee.
whyNot.2: 8.6 adds the $90 instead of subtracting it: 985 ÷ 115.

C.why: Distribute −3 to both terms: −6x + 15 = 39. Subtract 15: −6x = 24. Divide by −6: x = −4. Check: −3(−8 − 5) = −3(−13) = 39. ✓

whyNot.0: 4 drops the negative sign when dividing 24 by −6.
whyNot.3: 9 combines both slips: −15 from the distribution and a lost sign in the division.

C.q: Using C = (5/9)(F − 32), what Fahrenheit temperature F equals 40°C? Round to the nearest tenth if needed.

whyNot.1: 129.6 adds 32 to 40 before multiplying by 9/5. Undo in reverse: multiply first, then add 32.
whyNot.2: 72 is the value of F − 32, one step short of F.
whyNot.3: 54.2 multiplies by 5/9 instead of its reciprocal 9/5, then adds 32.

C.q: Which value of x makes 6 − 2(x + 3) = −10 true?

whyNot.1: −5 loses the sign when dividing −10 by −2; a negative divided by a negative is positive.
whyNot.3: −5.5 subtracts 6 − 2 first (4(x + 3) = −10). Multiplication comes before subtraction.

reteach.title: Wrapping and unwrapping a gift
reteach.question: A gift goes in a box, then gets wrapped, then gets a bow. To open it, which comes off first? How does that match solving an equation?

blocks.body: Building an expression wraps the variable in layers. In 5x + 9, x is put in the box (× 5) and then wrapped (+ 9). To get x back you unwrap in reverse: take off the wrapping first (subtract 9), then open the box (divide by 5). Try to open the box while it is still wrapped and you tear things up, which is what happens when you divide only one term.

blocks.text: Whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other side, and to EVERY term on that side. A gift opened on one side only is still half wrapped.

explain.body: Each operation is undone by its inverse: addition by subtraction, multiplication by division. Undo the last operation first, so in 4x + 7 you deal with the + 7 before the × 4.

whyNot.1: 24 is the value of 4x, one step short of x.
whyNot.3: 0.75 divides only 31 by 4 (x + 7 = 7.75). Every term must be divided.

explain.body: The number outside the parentheses multiplies EVERY term inside: 5(x − 2) = 5x − 10. Watch signs: −3(2x − 5) = −6x + 15.

test.why: Distribute: 5x − 10 = 35. Add 10: 5x = 45. Divide by 5: x = 9. Check: 5(9 − 2) = 5(7) = 35. ✓

whyNot.0: 7.4 distributes the 5 to x only: 5x − 2 = 35, so 5x = 37.
whyNot.3: 45 is the value of 5x, one step short of x.

explain.body: To solve a formula for one letter, treat the other letters as numbers and undo operations in reverse order. For P = 2l + 2w: subtract 2l, then divide by 2.

test.q: The perimeter of a rectangle is P = 2l + 2w. Which expression gives w?
test.why: Subtract 2l from both sides: P − 2l = 2w. Divide both sides by 2: w = (P − 2l)/2.

whyNot.0: 2l is added on the right, so it is undone by subtracting, not adding.
whyNot.1: w is multiplied by 2, so the last step is dividing by 2, not multiplying.
whyNot.2: P − 2l equals 2w; it still has to be divided by 2.

explain.body: Put your answer back into the ORIGINAL equation. If both sides match, you are done. If not, look for a sign slip or an early stop. A check takes ten seconds on the calculator and catches most distractors.

test.q: Which value of x checks in the equation 2x − 9 = 15?

whyNot.0: 3 subtracts 9 instead of adding it (2x = 6). Check: 2(3) − 9 = −3, not 15.
whyNot.2: 24 is the value of 2x, one step short of x.
whyNot.3: −3 computes 9 − 15 = −6 for 2x; the 9 must be added to 15.
